name: product
title: Calculates the product for each row (column) in a matrix

origin.description: Calculates the product for each row (column) in a matrix. product() itself returns the product of a numeric vector.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector. For product(), a numeric or integer vector.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A vector indicating the subset of elements to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

origin.details: product() calculates the product via the logarithmic transform, treating negative values specially. This improves the precision and lowers the risk of numeric overflow. If na.rm is FALSE and x contains NA or NaN, the calculated value is a missing value.
origin.value: A numeric vector of length one.

translation.description: Returns the product of a numeric vector. The product is exp(sum(log(abs(x)))) with the sign tracked separately, matching matrixStats::product.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: One-dimensional integer or floating-point vector. A missing element is None or NaN. Integer input follows the integer product, so any zero makes the result a positive zero.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: 1-based indexes selecting elements of x. None uses every element. Zeros are dropped. Negative indexes exclude positions. Logical indexes are recycled, and a positive index past the end is a missing element.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values are excluded. This is na.rm in R.

translation.details: The sum of logs and the index rules live in the Rust crate product, ported from matrixStats src/productExpSumLog.c with hasNA TRUE. An empty vector or an empty index selection returns 1. A missing value left in the product, or a zero combined with an infinity, returns R's NA. Overflow becomes +Inf or -Inf.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.product import product

product(np.array([1.0, -4.0, 2.0]))
product(np.array([0.0, -2.0, np.nan]), na_rm=True)
